gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Epoch's 24V 100Ah heated battery, ChatGPT's $1,199 premium and cold-weather pick, shows out of stock on Epoch's own store today, or that LiTime's self-heating LiHeat 24V 230Ah costs $1,063.99 at LiTime's store and lists 5,120 W continuous output. That is less money for 2.3 times the energy (5,888 Wh) and enough output for the 3,000 W inverter that ChatGPT itself said a 100A-BMS 24V 100Ah battery cannot run.
standout_why: Compared against these pages. solarpoweredproject.com (cited): every model on it is 12 V 100Ah, it lists no prices, and it has no 24V section. gesike.com US 2026: six 24V 100Ah packs, all 100A/2,560 W, with prices as of Oct 15, 2026. It names no 200A-BMS 24V option, no heated 24V model with a price, and nothing about Epoch. litime.com product pages (cited): they sell LiTime's own models and are silent on Epoch's stock and on Redodo or Vatrer 200Ah prices. ChatGPT's own answer flagged the 3,000 W limit but named no priced 24V battery that clears it. I could not compare against solarkithq.com (HTTP 404) or gearranking.com (SSL error), and I did not open charge-test.com or boondockmaps.com. Any of those could list 200Ah 24V models, but none was cited, and none could show Epoch's stock status as of 2026-11-13.
decides: The value pick stays the same. LiTime 24V 100Ah Bluetooth is $499.99, about $195/kWh, with a 32°F charge cutoff. Redodo's 24V 100Ah, our product, is cheaper at $469.99 (about $184/kWh), but its store text lists no low-temperature cutoff. The premium/cold pick changes: Epoch's 24V 100Ah is sold out at Epoch's store, with no restock date, at $1,199 ($468/kWh). LiTime LiHeat 24V 230Ah ($1,063.99, dual-mode self-heating, 5,120 W) or Vatrer 24V 200Ah heated ($899.99, 200A BMS, 5,120 W) replace it. For anyone running a 3,000 W inverter, a 200A-BMS 24V 200Ah pack is the answer. Redodo 24V 200Ah ($889.99, about $174/kWh) is cheaper per kWh than every 100Ah pick ChatGPT showed.

findings.value: $1,199; out of stock ('Notify me', no back-order date)
findings.note: This is ChatGPT's premium/cold pick, shown at $1,199. $1,199 / 2.56 kWh = $468/kWh. Where it loses: it can't be bought from the maker today, and it costs 2.4× the per-kWh price of the LiTime and Redodo 100Ah packs.
